findings.source_quote: λέγω δὲ καὶ περὶ τούτου οὗ εἴρηκεν „οὐδεὶς ἔγνω τὸν πατέρα“.
findings.english_quote: I am also speaking about this statement he made: ‘No one knew the Father.’
findings.issue: The draft resolves τούτου as referring to a statement. This is defensible if οὗ is understood as a genitive relative attracted to its antecedent, but a material alternative remains: “this one of whom he said,” referring to the Father and potentially connecting him with the previously mentioned unknown power. Neither existing note preserves that alternative or explains the choice. This is an interpretive ambiguity in the supplied wording, not evidence of source corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note explaining both constructions: “The main text understands τούτου as ‘this [statement]’ and οὗ as an attracted relative, ‘which he uttered,’ because the surrounding clauses discuss Jesus’ utterance and the quotation supplies its content. Alternatively: ‘I am also speaking about this one of whom he said, “No one knew the Father,”’ with a personal referent, potentially linking the Father with the unknown power.” The amended draft requires fresh review; no source correction is proposed.
